cues.text: Thank you for joining me for this brief
video that will walk you through the
process for adding a library plate model
to the ArtelWare application for use
with the Artell MVS system. Let's go
ahead and get started. ArtelWare
provides the user the ability to add
plate types that may not be Artell
verification plates. It should be noted
that only the usage of Artell
verification plates will provide NIS
traceable results. When considering
plates to be used with the MVS system,
they must be optically clear, flat
bottomed, and untreated. In addition,
you should also know whether or not
plate well itself is a round or square
well. You also need to know the top
diameter, the bottom diameter, as well
as the height in order to add it to our
TWear. Let's go ahead and walk through
adding two different plate types to our
Telware. The first plate type I'm going
to use is the Corning 3631,
which is an optional 96 well library
plate. Within our Telware, navigate to
the administration menu. From here,
navigate to the device cataloges menu
and click on the plate catalog tab.
Click on the view catalog box. You'll
notice that I currently do not have any
plates that are already added to the
plate catalog. Let's go ahead and click
on the add new plate model to catalog
icon. As I mentioned, today I'm adding a
Corning 3631 plate. I'll populate all of
the fields that have red asterisks,
including the manufacturer, the model,
the description of the plate, the plate
type, as well as whether or not the
plate well itself is a round well or a
square well. In this case, the Corning
3631 is a round well plate. I know my
top diameter, my bottom diameter, and
the height of my well because I've
gotten these from the plate manufacturer
specifications. Let's go ahead and click
the add box. And now we can see that we
have the 96 well Corning 3631 plate
that's added to the plate library.
Let's go ahead and click on add new
plate model to catalog.
It should be noted that unless you have
the 384 well plate support add-on
license, you will not be able to add any
384 well plates to the plate library.
I've gone ahead and added the Corning
384 well plate to the plate library. The
Corning 3762 plate is an optional 384
well library plate. I've gone ahead and
populated the manufacturer, the model,
and the description fields. In the plate
type field, I've selected 384 well
because again, I have the 384 well plate
support add-on added to our TWware. In
addition, this is a square well plate.
So, I've gone ahead and selected square
well. I've populated the top width, the
bottom width, and the height
specifications for this plate type. Now,
it's important to note that the Corning
3762 plate specifications that come from
Corning have been modified. Through our
experience, we've identified that these
plate specifications more accurately
reflect how the plate is designed. Let's
go ahead and select add and we'll click
okay. So now if we go back and review
the catalog again, we can click on the
drop down for the manufacturer and we
can see that we have a Corning 3631
plate and a Corning 3762
384 well plate. That concludes my brief
video. Do you have any questions? You
can contact our technical support team
option3 or at supportic
companies.com.
Thank you.
